name: Odd Mineral Resource
description: In Homer's country, there are $$$n$$$ cities numbered $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$ and they form a tree. That is, there are $$$(n-1)$$$ undirected roads between these $$$n$$$ cities and every two cities can reach each other through these roads. Homer's country is an industrial country, and each of the $$$n$$$ cities in it contains some mineral resource. The mineral resource of city $$$i$$$ is labeled $$$a_i$$$. Homer is given the plans of the country in the following $$$q$$$ years. The plan of the $$$i$$$-th year is described by four parameters $$$u_i, v_i, l_i$$$ and $$$r_i$$$, and he is asked to find any mineral resource $$$c_i$$$ such that the following two conditions hold: mineral resource $$$c_i$$$ appears an odd number of times between city $$$u_i$$$ and city $$$v_i$$$; and $$$l_i \leq c_i \leq r_i$$$. As the best friend of Homer, he asks you for help. For every plan, find any such mineral resource $$$c_i$$$, or tell him that there doesn't exist one.
input_specification: The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \leq n \leq 3 \cdot 10^5$$$) and $$$q$$$ ($$$1 \leq q \leq 3 \cdot 10^5$$$), indicating the number of cities and the number of plans. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \leq a_i \leq n$$$). Then the $$$i$$$-th line of the following $$$(n-1)$$$ lines contains two integers $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$ ($$$1 \leq x_i, y_i \leq n$$$) with $$$x_i \neq y_i$$$, indicating that there is a bidirectional road between city $$$x_i$$$ and city $$$y_i$$$. It is guaranteed that the given roads form a tree. Then the $$$i$$$-th line of the following $$$q$$$ lines contains four integers $$$u_i$$$, $$$v_i$$$, $$$l_i$$$, $$$r_i$$$ ($$$1 \leq u_i \leq n$$$, $$$1 \leq v_i \leq n$$$, $$$1 \leq l_i \leq r_i \leq n$$$), indicating the plan of the $$$i$$$-th year.
output_specification: Print $$$q$$$ lines, the $$$i$$$-th of which contains an integer $$$c_i$$$ such that $$$c_i = {-1}$$$ if there is no such mineral resource that meets the required condition; or $$$c_i$$$ is the label of the chosen mineral resource of the $$$i$$$-th year. The chosen mineral resource $$$c_i$$$ should meet those conditions in the $$$i$$$-th year described above in the problem statement. If there are multiple choices of $$$c_i$$$, you can print any of them.
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1479D — Odd Mineral Resource [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
